E. coli fluorescence stress screen

Source: vignettes/ecoli-fluorescence-stress-screen.Rmd
ecoli-fluorescence-stress-screen.Rmd

This article documents how DStressR can be used for a fluorescence/OD reporter-stress experiment. The example is based on the Dryad data associated with Dash et al. (2024), mSystems, which contain time-resolved GFP and OD measurements for E. coli global-regulator reporters under weak-stress conditions.

The Dash/Dryad raw data are not shipped with the package. The complete local workflow is kept in the repository under analysis/dryad_global_regulators/. After downloading and unzipping the Dryad archive, the expected local layout is:

analysis/dryad_global_regulators/raw/Data/

The main script for the windowed weak-stress analysis is:

Rscript analysis/dryad_global_regulators/run_weak_stress_window_calibrated_pipeline.R

Analysis Table

The weak-stress fluorescence time series are summarized into GFP AUC values and matched OD AUC values. The analysis table should use source-appropriate column names. In this dataset, the DStressR perturbation variable is a stress, not a drug or compound.

weak_stress <- read.delim(
  "analysis/outputs/dryad_global_regulators/dryad_weak_stress_windows_calibrated_alpha_input.tsv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

weak_stress$stress <- weak_stress$compound
weak_stress$compound <- NULL

names(weak_stress)

The reporter unit can be a biological reporter or a derived reporter-window unit. For the analysis used during manuscript development, each base reporter is crossed with a time window:

weak_stress$pseudo_reporter <- paste(
  weak_stress$promoter,
  weak_stress$window,
  sep = " | "
)

DStressR Model

The response model maps the Dash data to the generic DStressR interface by using reporter = "pseudo_reporter" and perturbation = "stress". Standard growth is the reference condition. The fluorescence signal is represented by gfp_auc, and growth by od_auc.

alpha <- read.delim(
  "analysis/outputs/dryad_global_regulators/dryad_weak_stress_windows_calibrated_alpha_supplied.tsv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
stress_alpha <- setNames(alpha$alpha_calibrated, alpha$pseudo_reporter)

assay <- prepare_assay(
  weak_stress,
  reporter = "pseudo_reporter",
  perturbation = "stress",
  control = "Standard",
  lux = "gfp_auc",
  growth = "od_auc",
  growth_exponent = stress_alpha,
  replicate = "replicate"
)

fit <- fit_destress(
  assay,
  technical = "replicate",
  empirical_bayes = TRUE,
  adjustment = "by_reporter",
  interaction = FALSE
)

tab <- results(fit)
hits <- call_hits(
  tab,
  fdr = 0.05,
  effect = "specific_effect",
  padj = "specific_padj_by_reporter"
)

The same workflow can be run with growth_exponent = 1 when the goal is to match a GFP/OD-style response more directly. The calibrated-alpha analysis shows how DStressR can use additional no-stress growth-transition data to estimate the response scale, while the weak-stress subset is used for inference.

Reproducibility Scripts

The repository scripts write intermediate inputs, fitted results, p-value histograms, volcano plots, and effect heatmaps under:

analysis/outputs/dryad_global_regulators/

The most relevant scripts are:

analysis/dryad_global_regulators/run_weak_stress_window_pipeline.R
analysis/dryad_global_regulators/run_weak_stress_window_calibrated_pipeline.R
analysis/dryad_global_regulators/run_weak_stress_window_rank1_adjustment.R
analysis/dryad_global_regulators/plot_weak_stress_three_target_inference.R

This example is intentionally different from the Binsfeld reporter-drug screen: it illustrates a small structured fluorescence/OD reporter-stress design rather than a large chemical library.
